small_guidance:
- The innermost `ic` loop is only 3 iterations; consider moving `ic` outside `kw` and using a single contiguous load of all 3 input channels per (kd,kh,kw,od,oh,ow) tuple via vectorized loads, since IC=3 is small and channel stride is the dominant contiguous axis after reordering input to NDHWC.
- Add autotune configs with smaller `BLOCK_SP` (e.g. 8) and try `num_stages=4` at BLOCK_SP=32/64 — the inner loop has 27*3*8=648 unrolled MACs, so register pressure is high and smaller tiles may improve occupancy.
- Hoist the per-(kd,kh,kw) constant index math (`PAD_D - kd`, `PAD_H - kh`, `PAD_W - kw`) and the validity-of-od/oh checks (which depend only on pd,ph,kd,kh, not on pw) outside the `ww`/pw_offs vector dimension to reduce per-lane work.
large_guidance:
- Reformulate as an im2col-style GEMM where each program handles one (n, pd, ph, pw-tile) and the reduction axis K = IC*KD*KH*KW*8 (the 8 sub-positions of the pool window). Use `tl.dot` over (BLOCK_SP × BLOCK_OC) tiles with explicit K-blocking — this exploits tensor cores and dramatically beats the current scalar FMA accumulation of 648 unrolled MACs.
- Try a "gather-scatter" alternative: one program per (n, ic, id, ih, iw-tile) that scatters input*weight contributions into the (pd, ph, pw, oc) pooled output via atomic adds — this avoids the modular-arithmetic masking in the current scheme and turns the conv-transpose into a natural scatter, which is the canonical formulation.
- Move to NDHWC (channels-last) layout for both input and output so the OC and IC axes are contiguous; the current NCDHW layout makes the K-dimension of the implicit GEMM strided, hurting load coalescing.
